01 · Brief and exact prompts

The original request defined the story, ink-wash aesthetic, music, TTS requirement, and bilingual subtitles. The production interpreted this as a short narrative film with a suspenseful rain passage followed by a warm reunion.

Original user prompt — verbatim

做一个《小蝌蚪找妈妈》的水墨动画，添加合适的音乐，请务必做到引人入胜，如果需要用到旁白或对话，用TTS合成，字幕用中英双语

ImageGen background prompt — verbatim

Generated once with transparent_background=false. The empty-water composition leaves room for animated characters.

Create a gorgeous cinematic wide 16:9 traditional Chinese ink wash painting background for a children's animation about tadpoles finding their mother. Empty pond setting ONLY, no animals, no tadpoles, no frogs, no text. Warm ivory rice paper texture, expressive sumi-e ink bleeding and delicate moss-green watercolor lotus leaves, a few pale blush lotus blossoms, graceful reeds at far left and far right, misty distant willow shoreline upper fifth. Composition: lots of airy pale open water in center and lower two thirds for animated characters. Rich authentic handmade brush texture, poetic tranquil spring morning, restrained elegant fine art, soft layered gray ink reflections, generous negative space. Full bleed landscape frame, no borders.

ImageGen character-sheet prompt — verbatim

Generated once with transparent_background=true. These painted characters replaced the preliminary geometric sprites in the final film.

Asset type: transparent sprite sheet for a traditional Chinese ink wash children's animation. Paint FOUR separate animals arranged in a precise 2 columns by 2 rows grid, each entirely contained within its quadrant with generous empty margins and no overlap. TOP LEFT: mother duck facing right, side view, elegant ivory and pale ochre wash with fluid black brush wing and orange beak. TOP RIGHT: golden orange carp facing right, side view, flowing translucent fins and a large kind eye. BOTTOM LEFT: friendly turtle facing right, side view, moss green shell with expressive ink hexagons and four visible short legs. BOTTOM RIGHT: smiling mother frog, front view, moss green ink wash, two large kind eyes, pale belly, four legs in crouched pose. The characters should be expressive and charming, unmistakably HAND PAINTED INK WASH with dry brush texture, diluted watercolor blooms, irregular brush edges, subtle paper-like grain inside colored areas, black ink accents. Fine Chinese picture book art with white spaces left inside forms. NO smooth flat vector shapes, NO glossy 3d, NO text, NO pond, NO leaves, NO ground, NO cast shadow. Transparent background. All characters similar visual size. Four individual animals only.

There was no separate video-model or music-generation prompt. Video frames were rendered in Python. Music was synthesized with NumPy. The exact TTS input texts are listed in the dialogue table below; English text appears in subtitles only.

02 · Narrative and final scene previews

The recurring question builds anticipation. Each animal contributes a recognizable clue: big eyes, four legs, and a green coat. The rain sequence creates uncertainty while the tadpoles stay together. The frog’s appearance resolves the clues and restores the warmer mood. Times below mark scene activation, which begins one second before that scene’s first spoken line.

01 · 00:00.00

初醒 / A new world

Establish spring and introduce the six tadpoles.

02 · 00:15.15

一问 / Mother Duck

Introduce the question and the clue: two big eyes.

03 · 00:34.10

再问 / The golden carp

A mistaken identification adds the clue: four legs.

04 · 00:46.95

线索 / Four little legs

The turtle supplies the final clue: a green coat.

05 · 01:00.07

风雨 / Stay together

Darken the pond, add rain, cluster the tadpoles, and lower the score.

06 · 01:18.18

回声 / A familiar voice

Reveal the frog beneath a lotus leaf and bring the tadpoles closer.

07 · 01:35.48

团圆 / Home

Show little legs, return to warmth, and finish with a message about love.

03 · Implementation

Generated artworkChinese TTS clipsMeasured audio timelineMusic + rain synthesisPillow frame renderingFFmpeg MP4 encoding

Visual composition and motion

  • Rendering: Pillow draws 1280 × 720 RGB frames at 24 fps. The generated pond is resized using Lanczos and given a subtle animated affine zoom of 1.000–1.012×.
  • Character extraction: the transparent sheet is cropped using adjusted normalized regions: duck (0, 0, .485, .54), fish (.485, 0, 1, .54), turtle (0, .54, .55, 1), frog (.55, .54, 1, 1). Alpha bounding boxes trim empty margins. Each character fits within 390 × 285 pixels on a 420 × 310 transparent canvas; scaled versions are cached.
  • Tadpoles: six procedural ink-colored bodies swim along scene-specific paths. Each tail uses 22 points and 21 tapering strokes; a sinusoidal phase varies per tadpole and frame. Small legs are drawn in the final scene.
  • Animal animation: the duck, three smaller ducklings, carp, and turtle use position, vertical bobbing, and slight rotation. The frog rises into view over two seconds. During the reunion, tadpoles approach over ten seconds.
  • Environment: seven elliptical water rings expand and fade. The rain scene adds 70 animated streaks and a dark overlay; later scenes add a gentle warm overlay. The sheltering lotus leaf is drawn procedurally.
  • Titles: a five-second opening title and final message are drawn over the pond. Chapter labels sit on a translucent panel. Chinese subtitle text is 32 px and English is 22 px on a pale translucent panel.

TTS voices and timing

RoleVoiceRatePitch
Narratorzh-CN-XiaoxiaoNeural−8%+0 Hz
Tadpoleszh-CN-XiaoyiNeural+0%+6 Hz
Adult animals / motherzh-CN-XiaoxiaoNeural−12%−3 Hz

edge-tts creates and caches 17 MP3 clips. Existing clips are reused; new synthesis is retried up to three times. FFmpeg decodes clips to mono 44.1 kHz float PCM, and their sample counts determine the dialogue timing. Speech begins at 5.0 seconds. Each line is followed by 1.3 seconds; scene changes add a further 1.3 seconds. The film duration is approximately 113.532 seconds before container rounding.

Original music and sound design

  • Melody: a repeating pentatonic sequence of MIDI notes [74, 77, 79, 81, 79, 77, 74, 72, 69, 72, 74, 77, 74, 72, 69, 67], triggered every 1.65 seconds. Lower accompanying notes cycle through [50, 53, 57, 60].
  • Sound synthesis: plucked timbres combine five exponentially decaying sine harmonics. The flute-like layer combines a fundamental and second harmonic with slow modulation and amplitude envelopes. These are synthesized timbres rather than recordings of acoustic instruments.
  • Emotional change: rain-scene melody notes move down one octave; their amplitude falls from 0.07 to 0.035, and the flute-like layer is omitted.
  • Speech balance: music is multiplied by 0.52 from 0.25 seconds before each line until 0.4 seconds after it. These gain changes are step changes, not interpolated fades. Voice gain is 0.85.
  • Rain: short decaying Gaussian-noise bursts occur every 0.18 seconds during the rain scene; the random seed is 17.
  • Master: stereo 44.1 kHz, 16-bit PCM WAV, with a two-second opening fade and four-second closing fade. The mixed waveform is bounded to ±0.95 before PCM conversion. No existing song recording was used.

Subtitle synchronization

The 17 Chinese/English pairs share the measured TTS timeline. Both languages are burned into the video; the separate UTF-8 SRT is also generated. The in-video caption persists 0.4 seconds after speech; the SRT cue persists 0.3 seconds after speech. The dialogue table records speech start/end times, before these caption extensions.

Encoding settings

Input frames: raw RGB24, 1280x720, 24 fps
Video: libx264 · preset fast · CRF 19 · yuv420p
Audio: AAC · target 192 kb/s · 44.1 kHz stereo
Container: MP4 · +faststart
Target duration: 113.53215419501133 seconds

This is a 2D composited animation: painted cutout animals plus procedural tadpole and environmental motion. Animal mouths and limbs are not individually rigged, and there is no lip synchronization or English voice track.

05 · Validation and observed results

  • All seven scene previews were visually inspected for character cropping, composition, and subtitle visibility.
  • All 17 voice files were present. Every cue contained both languages, and speech intervals were in order without overlap.
  • The mixed PCM audio had a measured peak of approximately 0.577 full scale and RMS of 0.065. No samples reached 0.99 full scale.
  • The final MP4 was decoded in full using FFmpeg without decoder errors. An encoded-frame screenshot was also inspected.
  • The final probe reported 1:53.54 duration, H.264 High profile, 1280 × 720, 24 fps, and AAC stereo at 44.1 kHz.

Production dependencies

Python with Pillow and NumPy; edge-tts 7.2.8; imageio-ffmpeg 0.6.0 and its bundled FFmpeg executable. The additional packages were installed into animation_deps. Rendering used the Windows Microsoft YaHei font.

python ./output/tadpoles/make_film.py --preview
python ./output/tadpoles/make_film.py --audio-only
python ./output/tadpoles/make_film.py
python ./output/tadpoles/build_report.py

Run from the project root with the required Python environment. Cached voice clips allow the existing speech to be reused without new TTS requests. Regenerating absent voice clips requires network access. The production renderer still writes its MP4 under output/tadpoles; it does not overwrite the relocated root video. The original renderer has a Windows-specific font dependency, so another platform requires a suitable Chinese font configuration. The recorded validator checks the renderer’s output location.
